content.title: How Do Humans and Computers Make Decisions?
content.definition: Sequential Flow runs code line-by-line blindly. Conditional Flow gives the program a brain to test live data and choose different paths!
content.keyPoint: The Golden Rule: Input Data ➔ Evaluate Condition (True / False) ➔ Execute Matching Action

content.title: Anatomy of a Condition: Asking Questions in Code
content.definition: A Condition is simply a Yes/No question that answers strictly True or False (Boolean value).
content.note: 💡 Remember: Single '=' is for assigning a value (x = 5), while Double '==' is for asking a comparison question (x == 5)!

content.title: 1-Way Branching: The "if" Statement
content.definition: Executes an action ONLY IF the condition is met (True). If not met (False), Python skips it and continues normal flow.
points: 1. Colon (:): Required at the end of the if line.
2. Indentation (4 spaces): Groups all statements inside the if block.

codeSnippet.code:
# Screening patient body temp
temp = 38.8

if temp > 37.5:
    print('⚠️ Warning: High fever!')

print('Check completed.')

content.title: 2-Way Branching: The "if...else" Choice
content.definition: Mutual Exclusivity: Python faces a fork in the road with two opposite paths. It runs Path A if True, or Path B if False. Exactly ONE path will run!
points: 1. Mutual Exclusivity: Both paths can never run together.
2. No condition on 'else': It acts as the automatic fallback for all other cases.

content.title: Multi-Way Decision: The "if...elif...else" Ladder
content.definition: First Match Wins! Python tests conditions sequentially from top to bottom. As soon as one condition is True, it runs that block and immediately exits the ladder.
points: 1. Order Matters: Always place strictest / highest conditions first.
2. Sequential Evaluation: Subsequent conditions are skipped once a match is found.

content.title: Logical Operators & The Complete Truth Table (and, or, not)
content.definition: Use and, or, and not to combine multiple criteria in a single decision statement.

table.desc: True only if BOTH sides are True
True if AT LEAST ONE side is True

codeSnippet.code:
# University Scholarship Criteria
gpa = 3.8
has_violations = False

# Both criteria required (and)
if gpa >= 3.7 and not has_violations:
    print('🎉 100% Scholarship Awarded!')

content.title: Top 3 Student Pitfalls to Avoid
content.definition: Mastering these 3 pitfalls builds strong diagnostic and problem-solving skills in software engineering:

cards.title: ❌ 1. Single '=' inside if
cards.desc: Using = instead of == causes SyntaxError because it assigns rather than compares.
cards.example: Wrong: if x = 10:  |  Right: if x == 10:

cards.title: ❌ 2. Wrong elif Order
cards.desc: Placing a broad check first (like >= 50 before >= 85) intercepts all cases and hides top scores!
cards.example: Wrong: if score >= 50 first  |  Right: if score >= 85 first

cards.title: ❌ 3. Missing Colon or Indent
cards.desc: Forgetting the colon (:) or failing to indent causes IndentationError.
cards.example: Wrong: if score > 50  |  Right: if score > 50:
